card.name: Inside non-English agent-noun words
card.fires_on: Partway through long Spanish, Latin, French or Italian words, just before an agent ending such as -ador, -ista, -ator or -ores (e.g. pol|iniz|adas, cron|ista, product|ores).

modes.label: Romance-language word stems

modes.label: Latin and Latin-derived terms
modes.description: Partway through a Latin or Latin-derived word or phrase, before an ending like -um or -sors.
modes.example: The Septuagint derives its name from Latin versio septuaginta<< interpret>>um,"translation of the seventy interpreters

card.writes: It pushes toward agent-noun endings like -ators, -maker and writer, meaning a person or thing that does something.
card.plain: It fires inside foreign-language words where an ending meaning a doer, such as -ator or -ista, is likely to come next.
